We know that initial education only takes 8 years, but lasts a lifetime.
We have a world-class curriculum and deep & meaningful development priorities. They will learn both inside our walls and outside our classrooms. They will read, write and solve problems after kayaking down the canal and study the Southall Uprising after making a fire in our Forest School. We will learn together. We will grow together. We will struggle & succeed together.
We will make these some of the best years of their lives.
Come and See Three Bridges!
Choosing a school for your child is a big decision, and we think the best way to get to know Three Bridges is to come and see us for yourself.
We hold four Open Mornings, giving prospective families the opportunity to meet some of the Early Years team, look around the school, see us in action and find out more about life at Three Bridges before the application deadline.
This year's open events are:📅Tuesday 6th October at 9am📅Tuesday 10th November at 9am📅Tuesday 8th December at 2pm📅Tuesday 12th January at 9am
Can't make one of our Open Events?We'd still love to meet you. During the Autumn Term, prospective parents and carers are welcome to contact the school office to ask about arranging a tour. Schools are busy places, so we can’t guarantee that we’ll be able to offer every requested date or time, but we’ll always do our best to find an opportunity for you to visit.

pageCache.pageTitle: Three Bridges Primary School - Ethos, Values & Moral Purpose
pageCache.text:
Ethos, Values & Moral Purpose
We know that primary education only takes 8 years, but lasts a lifetime.
A Developing, Critical MindWe want your children to thrive at Three Bridges academically and achieve their full potential. They will learn new things and share their learning with one another. They will grow from challenge and support and learn to be critical of thoughts and ideas, knowledge and understanding, and most importantly, reflective towards themselves and the broader world. We want them to engage curiously, courageously and collaboratively with what is said and read, but also have the depth to challenge critically and communicate confidently for what might be missing from the narrative. We want them to develop into problem solvers, pathfinders and poetic thinkers. This isn’t easy and it’s rarely in a straight line. Excellence at Three Bridges stems from nurturing the whole person, through hard-earned accomplishment and sky high expectations. This is reflected deeply in what they learn and how they learn across our curriculum. We believe in developing their minds.
Eyes Wide Open, Hands OutstretchedAs they navigate their way through Three Bridges, they will encounter globality, multi-ethnicity, inclusivity and adventure woven into the very fabric of learning. We will encourage them to look at what’s behind them, what’s in front of them, what is all around them - and up to the sky. We want your children to uncover the servant leader within them, becoming people that truly value and care for other people regardless of their individual strengths and struggles. They will learn to balance and harmonize the delicate interaction of taking care of themselves - mind, body, soul - and prioritising the needs of others so we all succeed. They will be listeners, laughers, and leaders in their own lives and in the lives of others. We want their eyes wide open to the world so that they may make their own contribution on purpose - their own difference - with a moral compass that steers them towards building community, strengthening family, and deepening relationships. We believe in uncovering young people who have their eyes wide open to the world and hands outstretched to serve.
We spend a great deal of time working in collaboration with each other and partner schools. In an attempt to be our very best, we use these opportunities to learn and help others learn. We don’t have all the answers, but we do have a few steps in the right direction and know that being a great school is only possible in fellowship with other schools. Together, we strive to:

pageCache.pageTitle: Three Bridges Primary School - About Us
pageCache.text:
"This is a WORLD CLASS school" - World Class Schools QM
"An outstandingly HAPPY School" - Art of Brilliance
“The HAPPIEST school on earth” – The Guardian
"You are part of a FAMILY."
"You learn a lot and you make FRIENDS."
Three Bridges is an incredible school.
While we exceed the basic goals of creating very literate and numerate children, our aim is much bolder; we are invested deeply in developing 3 core concepts:
A Developing, Critical MindWe want your children to thrive at Three Bridges academically and achieve their full potential. They will learn new things and share their learning with one another. They will grow from challenge and support and learn to be critical of thoughts and ideas, knowledge and understanding, and most importantly, reflective towards themselves and the broader world. We want them to engage curiously, courageously and collaboratively with what is said and read, but also have the depth to challenge critically and communicate confidently for what might be missing from the narrative. We want them to develop into problem solvers, pathfinders and poetic thinkers. This isn’t easy and it’s rarely in a straight line. Excellence at Three Bridges stems from nurturing the whole person, through hard-earned accomplishment and sky high expectations. This is reflected deeply in what they learn and how they learn across our curriculum. We believe in developing their minds.
Eyes Wide Open, Hands OutstretchedAs they navigate their way through Three Bridges, they will encounter globality, multi-ethnicity, inclusivity and adventure woven into the very fabric of learning. We will encourage them to look at what’s behind them, what’s in front of them, what is all around them - and up to the sky. We want your children to uncover the servant leader within them, becoming people that truly value and care for other people regardless of their individual strengths and struggles. They will learn to balance and harmonise the delicate interaction of taking care of themselves - mind, body, soul - and prioritising the needs of others so we all succeed. They will be listeners, laughers, and leaders in their own lives and in the lives of others. We want their eyes wide open to the world so that they may make their own contribution on purpose - their own difference - with a moral compass that steers them towards building community, strengthening family, and deepening relationships. We believe in uncovering young people who have their eyes wide open to the world and hands outstretched to serve.
A Full, Strong and Healthy HeartWe know that the core of a world-class education is what’s developing on the inside of a child; not simply what they know and can remember, but who they become. Character is not created after a week or a month - it is uncovered little by little, day by day, in everything that we do. Developing genuine curiosity, wonder, and resilience takes work. Optimism in the face of adversity or kindness in spite of cruelty takes modeling and practice, intention and attention. We support the development of incredible young people: mind, body and soul. We take their physical development as important as their academic development and we nurture within them a love of life. We want them to grow up to love one another, animals and nature, the incredible scope of all living things and, most importantly, that they grow up learning to love themselves. We believe that every child should have a full, strong and healthy heart.
We pride ourselves on providing an environment characterised by Professional Capital and Moral Purpose. We hire the very best staff, provide them with excellent development opportunities, allow them to collaborate, research and innovate in order to make the best decisions for your children. We spend time leading learning in partnership with other schools because we believe that those relationships make us stronger.
Our work has been featured in a number of publications, including The Research Informed Teaching Revolution, Stop Talking About Wellbeing, Dame Reena Keeble's 'Best Practice in Primary', Teach Primary's 'Outstanding Schools', The Teacher, Primary School Management, Leadership Focus, Education Leadership and Management, John Hattie's Visible Learning: Feedback, @TeacherToolkit's Mark.Plan.Teach, Cultures of Staff Wellbeing and Mental Health in Schools & The Financial Times. The Guardian called us 'The Happiest School on Earth'.
The journey of education is life-long and we would be honoured to take a few steps with you.
Welcome to Three Bridges.

pageCache.pageTitle: Three Bridges Primary School - Our Partnership - Our Family
pageCache.text:
Our Partnership - Our Family
Thank you for taking a moment to step into our schools at the Southall Waterside Federation - two communities connected by place, purpose and a shared belief in what schools can be.
Three Bridges and Wolf Fields are different in history, context and character, but united by something deeper: a belief that schools are human places, and that children flourish when they feel known, loved, challenged and inspired.
Our federation mark takes its inspiration from the bridges and waterways that connect us. It reflects an idea that sits at the heart of our work:
Learning in community. Enlarging worlds.
We believe children learn best in strong, caring communities - through relationships with teachers, friends, families and the world around them. And we believe great schools should continually enlarge the worlds available to children: introducing them to new ideas, experiences, people and possibilities.
That means great teaching, but also warm relationships, playful spaces, rigorous thinking, rich experiences and wide-open opportunities.
You will see this in the small things: the way children are greeted by name, the conversations in corridors, the celebrations of effort and the quiet moments of reassurance when things feel hard. And you will see it in the bigger things: the curriculum we design, the experiences we create and the partnerships we build.
As Executive Principal, I have the privilege of working across both schools - learning from them, supporting them and helping them grow together. But the heartbeat of Three Bridges and Wolf Fields is in the classrooms, playgrounds and shared laughter; in the dedication of our staff, the generosity of our families and, most of all, in the children themselves.
Wherever your child is starting from, whatever their dreams or challenges, they belong here.
Together, we want to give them an extraordinary, ordinary school life - full of joy, learning, friendship and hope.
Learning in community. Enlarging worlds.
Welcome to Southall Waterside Federation.We’re so glad you’re with us.
Dr Jeremy HannayExecutive PrincipalSouthall Waterside Federation

pageCache.pageTitle: Three Bridges Primary School - Curriculum MAGIC
pageCache.text:
Curriculum MAGIC
Our curriculum is designed to uncover incredible young people who are equipped with essential skills and knowledge for success in the complex and interconnected world. Through engaging and dialogic learning experiences both inside the school and outside in the broader world, we aim to empower students to become active, kind, and responsible global citizens who can effectively analyze information, collaborate and connect with others, express themselves with confidence, think creatively, appreciate diverse cultures, uphold positive values, and utilize technology to connect and engage meaningfully with the world around them. By integrating these key principles throughout our curriculum, we strive to prepare students to navigate and thrive in an ever-evolving, interconnected society while embracing their unique identities and making positive contributions to their communities and beyond.
At Three Bridges, our curriculum is designed to bring out the MAGIC of primary school - and make these 'the best years of their lives':
While we have engaged in extensive work to create the content for a global, multi-ethnic and inclusive curriculum, the content we teach is no more important than the way in which we engage with children in the presence of that very same content. We believe that certain subjects should be taught explicitly, be scripted and led only by the expert teacher. This is how we learn to understand the connection between symbols and sounds, the foundation of early reading. We believe that other subjects are best engaged with through highly skilled facilitated learning, powerful models of oracy and dialogic talk, where the teacher is a better guide and pupils are better leaders.
Our curriculum is organised, designed and delivered to uncover 'The Best Years of Their Lives'
